content.value_statement: Claude Router users need a quick way to understand routing patterns and estimated savings. This skill reads the local stats file and formats totals, route mix, exceptions, and savings.
actual_capabilities: Reads the local Claude Router stats file when available.
Displays all-time query counts and route distribution percentages.
Shows tool-aware routing and orchestrated query counts.
Reports router exception counts for meta queries.
Summarizes estimated savings, delegation savings, and daily totals.
limitations: Requires access to ~/.claude/router-stats.json on the user's machine.
Does not collect or verify token usage outside the stats file.
Cost savings are estimates based on fixed model price assumptions.
Cannot display history if the router has not created the stats file.

use_cases.title: Review Daily Routing
use_cases.description: A developer checks today's routed queries, route mix, and savings after using Claude Router.

use_cases.title: Track Cost Savings
use_cases.description: A team lead reviews estimated savings before reporting router value to stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Inspect Router Behavior
use_cases.description: A power user compares fast, standard, deep, and orchestrated routing totals to tune router expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Show My Stats
prompt_templates.prompt: Use router-stats to display my Claude Router usage summary from the local stats file.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Savings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use router-stats and explain the estimated savings, delegation savings, and total savings in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Route Mix
prompt_templates.prompt: Use router-stats to show route distribution percentages and identify which route type dominates my usage.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Recent Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use router-stats to review today's stats, exception counts, orchestrated queries, and any missing fields.

output_examples.output: A formatted summary with total routed queries, route percentages, savings totals, and today's query count.
A plain-language explanation comparing estimated savings, delegation savings, and route distribution changes.
A short message that no stats are available if the local file does not exist.

best_practices: Review the local stats file path before granting read access.
Use savings numbers as estimates unless you independently verify token usage.
Run the skill after meaningful router usage so percentages are useful.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to inspect unrelated Claude configuration files.
Do not paste private stats into shared channels without review.
Do not treat estimated savings as audited billing data.

faq.question: Does this skill send data to a server?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the skill file. It only instructs the assistant to read a local stats file and format results.

faq.question: What file does it read?
faq.answer: It reads ~/.claude/router-stats.json when the user allows local file access.

faq.question: What happens if the file is missing?
faq.answer: The skill tells the assistant to report that no stats are available yet.

faq.question: Are savings exact billing values?
faq.answer: No. The skill presents estimates based on fixed model price assumptions and average query sizes.

faq.question: Can it show route percentages?
faq.answer: Yes. It calculates percentages for fast, standard, deep, and orchestrated routes when data is present.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in the report metadata.
